note: Q63 governs the DA params floors and the owner-set drain protection accepted in F04 §4, and pins them in both languages. Acceptance clauses (a) governed lower bounds and (b) owner-set drain protection are implemented in `onchain/aiken/validators/da-params-governor.ak` and measured by the groups below. Acceptance clause (c) — the partial-attestation rescue/refund path — was delivered later, under the Q62 lane that held the `onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/da-attestation-types.ak` lease, and its two groups are now measured rather than OPEN. The rescue adds a `RescueStrandedAttestation` mint constructor and a `BurnForRescue` spend constructor. Its authorization is a state condition and nothing else — no deadline, no quorum of its own, no new F04 value — and that condition is the exact complement of what `ApplyToStateQueue` requires: the attestation's pinned `committee_signers_hash` OR its pinned `da_threshold` must no longer equal the current authenticated DA params' governed value. An attestation freezes both at Init and apply demands both still match, so it is unrecoverable precisely when either has moved. Taking only the committee half — which the first draft did, and an adversarial review caught before commit — would have left a second silent strand, since the governor permits a threshold change over an unchanged committee: such an attestation could never apply and never be rescued, while `AddSignatures` kept accepting signatures that could never amount to anything, and its ADA would be locked for good. The complement is also not too permissive: whenever it holds the apply gate is unsatisfiable no matter how many further signatures are gathered, so the path can never take value from an attestation still in flight. Rescuable and appliable are complements, never both, and Q62's `strandedness-completeness` group measures that against the same attestation and governed params its apply rejection uses. The refund is bound to the attestation's own value less the burnt DAAT, and the burn is required to be the sole movement of that policy's tokens in the transaction, which is what the duplicate and cross-attestation rejections are derived from. No count here is a declaration count: every published number is recomputed from an executed runner report. Deployment consequence of the F04 §4 floor, recorded so it is not rediscovered in the field: because `max(2, ceil(2*1/3)) == 2 > 1`, a one-member DA committee (and likewise a one-member owner set) is now unrepresentable — there is no `da_threshold` such a committee could name — so every single-signer DA topology is invalid by construction and must move to at least two members.

floorTable.note: Quoting F04's floor text proves the decision record still says what Q63 cited; it does not prove either implementation computes it. This digest is the shared pin that does. Its authority is the verifier's own recomputation, not anything recorded here: the verifier derives `max(2, ceil(2n/3))` from an integer ceiling written independently of the `(2n+2)/3` form both implementations use, hashes the table, and asserts this value; the `floor-arithmetic-provenance` Vitest check hashes the table produced by the SDK's `governedThresholdFloor` and asserts the same value. A floor/ceil transcription error on either side breaks one of the two legs. The `expression` field below is free-text documentation for a reader — it is compared only for consistency with the F04 bound expressions and is not what gives the digest its force.

compiler.rule: Aiken test execution for this goal is fork-only: the stock v1.1.22 build that is the authority for compilation and applied validator hashes ships a codegen defect and takes hours over this tree, so it is used only for `aiken check --skip-tests`. The gate resolves the compiler from `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN` then `MIDGARD_FORK_AIKEN_BIN` (CI pins only the latter) and fails closed with ERR_AIKEN_BINARY_UNPINNED when neither is set, rather than falling through to whatever `aiken` is first on PATH. Whichever resolves must then report a `aiken v1.1.23` version or the run fails closed with ERR_AIKEN_COMPILER_MISMATCH, so a stock binary cannot supply a result under the fork's name. Both behaviours are seeded self-tests, not assurances: the gate spawns itself with the variables stripped, and again against a stub binary reporting a v1.1.22 version.

implementation.constantSplit: `min_governed_threshold` bounds a threshold, `min_owner_count` bounds a set size. The off-chain twin mirrors the split as `MIN_DA_GOVERNED_THRESHOLD` and `MIN_DA_OWNER_COUNT` so a change to either cannot silently move the other. The `owner_len >= min_owner_count` check is redundant under the current floor (a one-owner set already fails because `update_threshold` would have to be both >= 2 and <= 1) and is kept as declared defense in depth against a future weakening of the two-thirds term; the drain rejection test is named for the resulting overlap rather than claiming a single disposition.

groups.claim: The mint handler itself enforces the governed floors on the params output it authorises, so the governor cannot be initialised with below-floor params.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only by construction, and declared so. The claim is about a Plutus minting policy resolving the output it authorises; the SDK builds no DA-params initialisation transaction, so there is no off-chain twin that could carry this cardinality. This is the seam the parent-handoff claim about the node's single-key DA defaults being unmintable actually rests on, which is why it is measured separately from the spend seam.

groups.claim: The spend handler itself enforces the governed floors on the continuing output, so a quorum cannot rotate the params into a below-floor configuration.

The claim is about a Plutus spending handler resolving its own continuing output; the SDK builds no DA-params update transaction, so there is no off-chain twin that could carry this cardinality. Every other measured group is required to carry it in both languages.

The two sides are therefore measured to different depths, and the difference is deliberate rather than glossed: full-table off-chain (this group sweeps 0..max_indexed_signer_count and pins the digest), sample-pinned on-chain (`da_params_governor_invariant_da_threshold_majority_floor` pins a sample of set sizes that straddles the clamp boundary and reaches the top of the range at 100, 255 and 256). No full-table on-chain claim is made anywhere, because no full-table Aiken sweep exists.

groups.claim: A partially signed attestation stranded by a mid-flight committee rotation can be rescued/refunded.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only by construction, and declared so rather than left to be inferred from an absent citation. The claim is that a Plutus policy releases a stranded UTxO's value, which is settled only by running the `da_attestation` mint and spend handlers against a transaction; a Node verifier can execute no Plutus. The control therefore carries both handlers, because a rescue transaction is valid only if both run — the mint half decides whether the attestation is stranded and where its value goes, the spend half binds that particular UTxO to the decision, and pinning only the mint would leave the binding the replay rejection attacks unmeasured. The off-chain half of this work exists and is measured, but under Q62's gate and against different claims (redeemer ABI ordering, and the builder's refusal to rescue a live attestation), so it is not cited here as if it carried this cardinality.

groups.claim: The rescue path rejects theft of another party's attestation value, duplicate refunds, and replay of a consumed rescue.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only, for the same reason as the rescue path itself: each rejection is a Plutus handler refusing a transaction. Each is also a one-field mutation of the control's transaction, which is why they are measured against the same fixture rather than restated off-chain. Theft is the state-condition negative — the governed committee still equals the one the attestation froze, so the attestation is in flight and its value is not the rescuer's to take; without that condition the path would be a burn-and-take backdoor over every live attestation. Duplicate is the burn-quantity negative: because this policy is stateless it cannot prove per-header uniqueness, so two DAAT UTxOs may share an asset name, and retiring both under one authorization collapses to exactly the `-2` the sole-burn check refuses. Replay is the binding negative: the rescue mint redeemer names one input, so its authorization cannot be replayed onto a second attestation UTxO bundled into the same transaction.
